proposal.hypothesis: Switching from squared loss to Huber loss will reduce CEP90 in the outlier-heavy clustered_20 (53.5m) and collinear_15 (49.8m) slices by down-weighting the 25m outlier bias, while keeping clean_15 CEP90 within the allowed 10%/0.25m increase.
proposal.rationale: NLS overall CEP90 is 23.66m with failure rate 8.7%, driven by clustered_20 (CEP90 53.5m, 25% failures) and collinear_15 (CEP90 49.8m, 23% failures) at 20% outlier rate with 25m bias. Robust Huber loss should curb these outlier-driven tails; clean_15 CEP90 is only 1.75m so headroom is ample.

decision.reason: Accepted: CEP90 improved; median, failures, clean slices and numerical success passed.

model_traces.system_prompt:
You are a bounded applied-mathematics experiment planner, not a code writer.
Study static 2-D BLE target localization under noisy/helper-drift observations, not target motion detection.
Use ONLY validation metrics, worst slices, and the actual history below. Propose exactly one legal,
untried, effective configuration change with a falsifiable hypothesis tied to observed evidence.
The deterministic executor accepts only a reduction in overall CEP90, no failure-rate increase,
no >10% overall median degradation, no clean-slice CEP90 increase beyond max(10%, 0.25m),
and no >5 percentage point convergence decline. A rejected trial is useful evidence, not a failure to hide.
Do not invent results, alter data/scenarios, ask for held-out metrics, or request arbitrary execution.
Method meanings: nls=ordinary squared loss; huber/cauchy=robust losses without metadata;
weighted_nls=observable metadata only; adaptive=Huber fit with metadata and residual reweighting.
Temporal weighting is useful only when repeated observations suggest helper instability; it is NOT target tracking.
Metadata here is synthetic precision/age information independent of contamination labels. No oracle labels.
Allowed single changes: name in [huber,cauchy,adaptive,weighted_nls]; loss_scale_m in [4,6,8,10,12];
reliability_threshold in [0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4]; use_temporal_weight in [true,false];
max_irls_iterations in [6,10,14]. Scale affects only robust methods; threshold/iterations affect adaptive;
never choose an irrelevant control. Do not repeat any previously attempted full configuration.
Output one JSON object ONLY, with hypothesis (8-300 characters),
change {field: one allowed field, value: correctly typed allowed value},
and rationale (8-400 characters). Reason briefly from observed values, not a fixed schedule.

proposal.hypothesis: Switching from squared loss to Huber loss will reduce CEP90 in the outlier-heavy clustered_20 (53.5m) and collinear_15 (49.8m) slices by down-weighting the 25m outlier bias, while keeping clean_15 CEP90 within the allowed 10%/0.25m increase.
proposal.rationale: NLS overall CEP90 is 23.66m with failure rate 8.7%, driven by clustered_20 (CEP90 53.5m, 25% failures) and collinear_15 (CEP90 49.8m, 23% failures) at 20% outlier rate with 25m bias. Robust Huber loss should curb these outlier-driven tails; clean_15 CEP90 is only 1.75m so headroom is ample.

proposal.hypothesis: Tightening the Huber loss scale from 8m to 6m will further down-weight the 25m outlier bias, reducing overall CEP90 below 12.54m and shrinking the collinear_15 tail (CEP90 49.98m, 22.9% failures) without pushing clean_15 CEP90 above 1.92m.
proposal.rationale: Huber at scale 8 already cut overall CEP90 from 23.66m to 12.54m and failures from 8.7% to 4.5%, but collinear_15 (CEP90 49.98m) and clustered_20 (19.35m) remain outlier-dominated at 20% rate with 25m bias. A smaller scale sharpens outlier rejection; clean_15 CEP90 is only 1.75m, leaving ample headroom under the 10%/0.25m clean cap.

decision.reason: Rejected: validation CEP90 did not improve.

proposal.hypothesis: Tightening the Huber loss scale from 8m to 6m will further down-weight the 25m outlier bias, reducing overall CEP90 below 12.54m and shrinking the collinear_15 tail (CEP90 49.98m, 22.9% failures) without pushing clean_15 CEP90 above 1.92m.
proposal.rationale: Huber at scale 8 already cut overall CEP90 from 23.66m to 12.54m and failures from 8.7% to 4.5%, but collinear_15 (CEP90 49.98m) and clustered_20 (19.35m) remain outlier-dominated at 20% rate with 25m bias. A smaller scale sharpens outlier rejection; clean_15 CEP90 is only 1.75m, leaving ample headroom under the 10%/0.25m clean cap.

proposal.hypothesis: Switching from huber to cauchy loss at scale 8m will reduce overall CEP90 below 12.54m by more aggressively suppressing the 25m outlier bias, shrinking the collinear_15 tail (CEP90 49.98m, 22.9% failures) while keeping clean_15 CEP90 within 1.92m.
proposal.rationale: Huber at scale 8 cut CEP90 to 12.54m but collinear_15 (49.98m) and clustered_20 (19.35m) remain outlier-dominated; tightening scale to 6 was rejected (CEP90 rose to 12.81m). Cauchy's heavier-tailed redescending influence targets the 25m bias more strongly than a smaller Huber scale, without the scale-6 regression.

decision.reason: Rejected: validation CEP90 did not improve.

model_traces.system_prompt:
You are a bounded applied-mathematics experiment planner, not a code writer.
Study static 2-D BLE target localization under noisy/helper-drift observations, not target motion detection.
Use ONLY validation metrics, worst slices, and the actual history below. Propose exactly one legal,
untried, effective configuration change with a falsifiable hypothesis tied to observed evidence.
The deterministic executor accepts only a reduction in overall CEP90, no failure-rate increase,
no >10% overall median degradation, no clean-slice CEP90 increase beyond max(10%, 0.25m),
and no >5 percentage point convergence decline. A rejected trial is useful evidence, not a failure to hide.
Do not invent results, alter data/scenarios, ask for held-out metrics, or request arbitrary execution.
Method meanings: nls=ordinary squared loss; huber/cauchy=robust losses without metadata;
weighted_nls=observable metadata only; adaptive=Huber fit with metadata and residual reweighting.
Temporal weighting is useful only when repeated observations suggest helper instability; it is NOT target tracking.
Metadata here is synthetic precision/age information independent of contamination labels. No oracle labels.
Allowed single changes: name in [huber,cauchy,adaptive,weighted_nls]; loss_scale_m in [4,6,8,10,12];
reliability_threshold in [0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4]; use_temporal_weight in [true,false];
max_irls_iterations in [6,10,14]. Scale affects only robust methods; threshold/iterations affect adaptive;
never choose an irrelevant control. Do not repeat any previously attempted full configuration.
Output one JSON object ONLY, with hypothesis (8-300 characters),
change {field: one allowed field, value: correctly typed allowed value},
and rationale (8-400 characters). Reason briefly from observed values, not a fixed schedule.

proposal.hypothesis: Switching from huber to cauchy loss at scale 8m will reduce overall CEP90 below 12.54m by more aggressively suppressing the 25m outlier bias, shrinking the collinear_15 tail (CEP90 49.98m, 22.9% failures) while keeping clean_15 CEP90 within 1.92m.
proposal.rationale: Huber at scale 8 cut CEP90 to 12.54m but collinear_15 (49.98m) and clustered_20 (19.35m) remain outlier-dominated; tightening scale to 6 was rejected (CEP90 rose to 12.81m). Cauchy's heavier-tailed redescending influence targets the 25m bias more strongly than a smaller Huber scale, without the scale-6 regression.

proposal.hypothesis: Enabling temporal weighting on the huber scale-8 fit will reduce overall CEP90 below 12.54m by down-weighting helper-drift observations in the mobile_rate>0 slices (collinear_15 CEP90 49.98m, clustered_20 19.35m), while keeping clean_15 CEP90 within 1.92m.
proposal.rationale: Huber scale-8 gives CEP90 12.54m but collinear_15 (49.98m, 22.9% failures) and clustered_20 (19.35m) remain outlier-dominated; scale-6 and cauchy both raised overall CEP90 (12.81m, 13.14m). Temporal weighting targets repeated helper instability in these mobile slices without touching the clean slice.

decision.reason: Accepted: CEP90 improved; median, failures, clean slices and numerical success passed.

model_traces.system_prompt:
You are a bounded applied-mathematics experiment planner, not a code writer.
Study static 2-D BLE target localization under noisy/helper-drift observations, not target motion detection.
Use ONLY validation metrics, worst slices, and the actual history below. Propose exactly one legal,
untried, effective configuration change with a falsifiable hypothesis tied to observed evidence.
The deterministic executor accepts only a reduction in overall CEP90, no failure-rate increase,
no >10% overall median degradation, no clean-slice CEP90 increase beyond max(10%, 0.25m),
and no >5 percentage point convergence decline. A rejected trial is useful evidence, not a failure to hide.
Do not invent results, alter data/scenarios, ask for held-out metrics, or request arbitrary execution.
Method meanings: nls=ordinary squared loss; huber/cauchy=robust losses without metadata;
weighted_nls=observable metadata only; adaptive=Huber fit with metadata and residual reweighting.
Temporal weighting is useful only when repeated observations suggest helper instability; it is NOT target tracking.
Metadata here is synthetic precision/age information independent of contamination labels. No oracle labels.
Allowed single changes: name in [huber,cauchy,adaptive,weighted_nls]; loss_scale_m in [4,6,8,10,12];
reliability_threshold in [0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4]; use_temporal_weight in [true,false];
max_irls_iterations in [6,10,14]. Scale affects only robust methods; threshold/iterations affect adaptive;
never choose an irrelevant control. Do not repeat any previously attempted full configuration.
Output one JSON object ONLY, with hypothesis (8-300 characters),
change {field: one allowed field, value: correctly typed allowed value},
and rationale (8-400 characters). Reason briefly from observed values, not a fixed schedule.
